title: Rewriting India's Nutrition Story: Experts Call for Science Over Shortcuts
summary: At the third edition of the ETHealthworld Nutriwell Conclave, experts discussed India's nutritional challenges and the rise of dietary supplements. They emphasized the need for evidence-based nutrition and traditional dietary wisdom to combat these issues....

At the ETHealthworld Nutriwell Conclave 2026, the inaugural panel discussion, “Rewriting India’s Nutrition Story – Science Over Shortcuts,” brought together experts to examine India's evolving nutritional challenges, the rise of dietary supplements and the importance of evidence-based nutrition.Prof Pushpesh Pant, Indian food critic and historian, emphasised the relevance of traditional dietary wisdom, seasonal foods and balanced meals. He cautioned against excessive dependence on processed nutritional products while highlighting the importance of enjoying food.

Dr. Bani Tamber Aeri, Professor, Department of Food and Nutrition, Institute of Home Economics, Delhi University, highlighted three critical factors influencing metabolic disorders: dietary habits, sedentary lifestyles and stress. She advocated balanced nutrition, regular physical activity and healthy sleep patterns.

Advt

Dr. G.M. Subba Rao, Scientist-G, ICMR-NIN, explained that iron deficiency accounts for only a portion of India's anaemia burden. He emphasised dietary diversity, sanitation and micronutrient intake, advocating a shift from nutrient-centric approaches towards holistic food-based nutrition.

Dr. Sarath Gopalan, President, Nutrition Society of India, stressed that nutritional interventions must be scientifically validated, affordable and sustainable. He also highlighted the importance of effective regulatory implementation and communicating scientific findings to the public.Dr. Kashipa Harit, Joint Director, NABH, discussed integrating nutritional screening and counselling into clinical care, emphasising collaboration between doctors, dietitians and nursing professionals.

Joining the discussion, Rajit Punhani, CEO, FSSAI, highlighted the importance of ethical marketing, scientifically supported product claims and front-of-pack labelling.Moderated by Vikas Dandekar, Editor, Pharma & Healthcare, Economic Times Group, the discussion reinforced the need to prioritise scientific evidence, traditional dietary wisdom and informed consumer choices over nutritional shortcuts.

Key takeaways:

  • Prioritise dietary diversity and balanced nutrition.
  • Ensure scientific validation of nutritional interventions.
  • Strengthen regulatory implementation and ethical marketing.
  • Integrate preventive and therapeutic nutrition into clinical care.
  • Promote nutrition literacy and informed consumer choices.
  • Address nutritional misinformation across digital platforms.
